problem: Prior VLA-driven humanoid control relies on hand-crafted low-dimensional action vocabularies (root velocity, end-effector pose, keyframes) as the interface to a low-level controller, which limits expressiveness and prevents agile whole-body behaviors such as seated interactions. No vision-language whole-body benchmark or data exists that is sim-to-real ready.
motivation: Humanoids are high-dimensional dynamic systems that need slow semantic reasoning plus fast reactive control. A learned latent action vocabulary could cover diverse whole-body motions while carrying vision-language semantics. Kinematic replay of retargeted MoCap in photorealistic simulation provides cheap synthetic vision-language data without needing a dynamic controller.
key_idea: A hierarchical dual-process policy in which a CVAE-based vision-language model (System 2) outputs latent verbs that a separately RL-trained, DAgger-distilled proprioceptive whole-body controller (System 1) decodes into joint actions.
insight: Structured latent sampling and alignment matter: the naive deterministic hierarchical baseline (NS, no sampling) gets 7.5% overall vs 58.5% for LeVERB (7.8x). Removing the discriminator (ND) drops overall SR to 33.0, and vision-language navigation collapses because latents from language-only and vision-language demos separate. Removing latent sampling in System 1 (NLS) drops to 6.5, and dropping the high-level VL policy (NVL) gives 25.5 and near-failure on visual tasks. The kinematics encoder helps less (NE 53.0). A validation-loss ablation shows random latents fail to reconstruct future states, so the latent carries real information.
method: LeVERB-Bench data pipeline: replay retargeted MoCap kinematics in IsaacSim with ray tracing, randomize scene, object, camera and mirroring (154 trajectories x100 = 17.1 h), label with a VLM or manually. Add 2.7 h of language-only data (about 460-500 trajectories) with spatial cues injected into the text.

LeVERB-VL (System 2, 10 Hz): frozen SigLIP ViT-B/16 image encoders (ego + third-person) and text encoder, a Transformer backbone, and an MLP head predicting a latent Gaussian; current frame only, no history. 102.56M trainable parameters.

Residual CVAE: a privileged kinematics encoder on future states adds a residual to the VL prior mean (mu = mu_rho + mu_E). A decoder reconstructs future pose deltas from z and s_t. A KL term between posterior and VL prior aligns them.

Modality discriminator with gradient reversal: language-only data is fed white-noise images, and the discriminator with GRL makes latents invariant to whether an image is present, unifying the latent space.
Teachers: vision-language-agnostic PPO motion-tracking policies (DeepMimic-style rewards, domain randomization, early termination) on the Unitree G1.

LeVERB-A (System 1, 50 Hz): a 2-layer Transformer student trained by DAgger with Huber loss, taking proprioception and the latent as separate tokens. It is trained with latents sampled from the VL distribution, resampled every 5 steps to match the 10 Hz rate. At deployment it uses the mean latent. Frozen VL latents decouple training from rendering.
Deployment: System 1 runs onboard in C++/ONNX at 50 Hz. System 2 runs on an RTX 4090 and streams latents over ROS2.

setting.backbone: SigLIP ViT-B/16 (frozen) + Transformer CVAE VLA (System 2, trained from scratch on top) + Transformer student policy distilled from PPO teachers (System 1)
setting.training_data: Synthetic: 17.1 h photorealistic IsaacSim renderings of retargeted MoCap (154 trajectories x100 randomizations) plus 2.7 h language-only motions (~460-500 trajectories); 5,996 demos in the mixture (3,696 vision-language, 2,300 language-only). Sources include AMASS, LAFAN and in-house RL motions.
setting.observation: Egocentric head camera + randomized third-person camera RGB, text instruction, proprioception (joint positions and velocities, IMU, previous action)
setting.action_space: Latent verb z from System 2 at 10 Hz; joint position targets (torque-level PD) from System 1 at 50 Hz
setting.simulator: IsaacSim (ray-traced rendering; physics-based closed-loop eval); real Unitree G1
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged kinematics encoder and teacher observations are used only in training)

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 random unseen scene/instruction runs per task category
numbers.backbone: SigLIP + CVAE VLA + Transformer whole-body policy
numbers.extra: trained only on synthetic data; unseen material/object combinations
numbers.evidence: Table 1 All row: LeVERB 58.5 (ND 33.0, NE 53.0, NVL 25.5, NLS 6.5, NS 7.5)

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (LeVERB-Bench), not a standard nav benchmark. The text says average 58.9% while the table says 58.5. Real-world results are qualitative only (open-loop latent replay on G1). Other per-task numbers (VNR 30, VNS 5, Sit 100, Stand 90, Locomotion 100) are in Table 1 but not entered as separate rows.
results: On LeVERB-Bench, LeVERB reaches 58.5% overall success and 80% on simple visual navigation, versus 7.5% for the naive hierarchical baseline without sampling (7.8x). It also beats the no-discriminator (33.0), no-VL (25.5) and no-kinematics-encoder (53.0) ablations. Zero-shot sim-to-real on a Unitree G1 shows vocabulary generalization and visually conditioned sitting via open-loop latent replay.
limitations: Short prediction horizon with no long-term history or planning
No fast vision feedback loop in System 1, which limits agility and dexterous tasks
Real-world results are qualitative and open-loop replay of simulation-generated latents; hard tasks (turning around VNR, VNS sit) have low success rates in simulation (30, 5)
